strongest_objection: The declared type is narrower than the map, and the author says so in the text of two kept items. The `of` opens 'a mechanism by which a party builds, borrows, or fakes an alternative to the table it is at', but Cheap to claim, ruinous to check closes with 'there is no alternative and the leaving is the point', and Tied hands manufactures an inability to accept with no destination either; both are credible leavings, not alternatives. The author's own boundary case shows the fence that is actually being used: burned ships is out because it makes staying credible, and the items are in because they make leaving credible, with or without somewhere to go. So the repair is to the type sentence, not the items. Replace the opening clause with: 'A mechanism by which a party builds, borrows, or fakes an alternative to the table it is at, or a leaving that needs no alternative, named with ...' and leave the rest of the `of` unchanged; the seriation axis already lists the stops those two items occupy (a constraint on an absent owner's behalf, the checker's ruin), so nothing else moves. The same crack mis-sorts boundary_claim four, which lumps 'the precommitment' with burned ships: a precommitment to fight is out, a precommitment to leave (a floor announced to the press or the staff) is in-type and absent from the map. Beyond that I tried to collapse Fed suitor into Kettle on the hob and could not, found one cost slot filled with the exercise cost instead of the upkeep, one discriminator naming a thing that is not on the map, one charter-forgery claim asserted with a 'whenever' that the record does not support, one tell stated unconditionally that is only true when the counterparty can outlast the meter, and one incompatibility edge whose antecedent cannot fail as written and is false in the map's own ransom case.

items.item: Fed suitor: the alternative is a party with wants of its own, so the second supplier or the rival employer stays an option only while it is given something, a share of the volume, a real chance at the position, and stops quoting the third time it learns it was the stalking horse; the carrier is the suitor's patience; keeping it credible costs a dual-source tax, the ten or twenty percent of volume placed with the second source at a worse price, or the interviews one actually sits; the tell is how long the suitor has been in place and what it has received, since a second source at zero share for three years is a name and not an option; the fake that survives is the suitor who knows and stays because it is paid to, which is the Paid floor by another door; not Qualified on paper, where the certificate needs no one's consent and decays with the spec, since here the option decays with a person's willingness.
items.why: Left of my closest pair; survives (see neighbor_test). 'The third time it learns it was the stalking horse' is an illustrative count, not a finding, and reads as one.

items.item: Kettle on the hob: the alternative is a relationship kept at a temperature, as the acquirer's corporate-development team met every quarter so that 'we have inbound interest' stays true, and each meeting costs the founder a slice of information and gives the acquirer a free look; the carrier is the cadence of contact; keeping it credible costs the leak, since a kettle kept warm is being read, and the acquirer is keeping the founder warm as its own option, so the two parties are each other's walkaway and neither knows which of them is the real one; the tell is depth, whether the acquirer's engineers have looked at the code or only its dealmakers have had coffee, and who proposed the last meeting; the fake that survives is inbound interest that was a form letter, since an investor cannot call the acquirer without telling it there is a deal; not the competing sheet, a paper with a date, since the kettle has no paper and no date, only a temperature.
items.why: Right of my closest pair. Its discriminator says 'not the competing sheet', which is not an item on this map, and misses its real nearest neighbor, Fed suitor, from which it separates only on what is fed (the deal's currency, countable by the incumbent, versus information about the holder, invisible to the counterparty). The mechanism is kept whole; only the discriminator is replaced.
items.repair: Kettle on the hob: the alternative is a relationship kept at a temperature, as the acquirer's corporate-development team met every quarter so that 'we have inbound interest' stays true, and each meeting costs the founder a slice of information and gives the acquirer a free look; the carrier is the cadence of contact; keeping it credible costs the leak, since a kettle kept warm is being read, and the acquirer is keeping the founder warm as its own option, so the two parties are each other's walkaway and neither knows which of them is the real one; the tell is depth, whether the acquirer's engineers have looked at the code or only its dealmakers have had coffee, and who proposed the last meeting; the fake that survives is inbound interest that was a form letter, since an investor cannot call the acquirer without telling it there is a deal; not Fed suitor, which is paid in the deal's own currency, a share of volume or an interview actually sat, where the incumbent can count what it lost, since the kettle is paid in information about the holder that the counterparty never sees on any ledger.

items.item: Second table in the square: the walkaway from the private table is a public one, the activist's open letter, the employees' petition, the leak, and it is credible in proportion to an audience that would care and a party that has published before; the carrier is the audience; keeping it credible costs the private table, since a letter once sent ends the negotiation it threatened, so the option is one-shot and the party that uses it has no second letter; the tell is whether the audience exists and can hurt, a following, a reporter's number, a prior letter that landed, and a drafted letter shown privately is the tell of a party that would rather not send it; the fake that survives is the audience the counterparty overestimates, since the counterparty cannot poll the crowd before the letter goes; not Higher court's door, which appeals to a superior with jurisdiction, since the square has none and cannot be bought.
items.why: The upkeep slot is filled with the exercise cost. 'Keeping it credible costs the private table' is what sending the letter costs, not what keeps the option credible before it is sent; the item's own tell says credibility is 'a prior letter that landed', so the upkeep is earlier tables lost. The one-shot insight is preserved and now sits where it belongs.
items.repair: Second table in the square: the walkaway from the private table is a public one, the activist's open letter, the employees' petition, the leak, and it is credible in proportion to an audience that would care and a party that has published before; the carrier is the audience; keeping it credible costs earlier tables, since the audience that would care is built by letters already sent, each of which ended the private negotiation it threatened, so the option is one-shot at any table and its credibility at this one is bought with tables lost before; the tell is whether the audience exists and can hurt, a following, a reporter's number, a prior letter that landed, and a drafted letter shown privately is the tell of a party that would rather not send it; the fake that survives is the audience the counterparty overestimates, since the counterparty cannot poll the crowd before the letter goes; not Higher court's door, which appeals to a superior with jurisdiction, since the square has none and cannot be bought.

items.item: Higher court's door: the walkaway is an appeal to a table above this one, bought from the higher power, as the medieval borough's charter let the town's disputes go to the king's court rather than the lord's, and as an arbitration clause or a regulator's complaint line does now; the carrier is the grant, recorded and paid for; keeping it credible costs the higher party's fee and its continuing interest in having the lower party as a client, so the door closes when the crown stops needing the town; the tell is the record of the grant and whether the door has ever been used; the fake that survives is the forged charter, which monastic houses produced in quantity and which the crown honored whenever the forgery's side was the side it preferred, so a fake stands as long as the verifier wants it to be real; not register-jumps' carriers, which move a live situation into a new register, since here the jump is only threatened and its credibility is a document in a chest.
items.why: An illustrative case asserted as documented history: monastic charter forgery at scale is well attested, but 'the crown honored whenever the forgery's side was the side it preferred' is a universal the record does not support and the mode note only calls 'simplified'. Softened to 'often enough', which is all the mechanism (a fake stands as long as the verifier wants it real) needs.
items.repair: Higher court's door: the walkaway is an appeal to a table above this one, bought from the higher power, as the medieval borough's charter let the town's disputes go to the king's court rather than the lord's, and as an arbitration clause or a regulator's complaint line does now; the carrier is the grant, recorded and paid for; keeping it credible costs the higher party's fee and its continuing interest in having the lower party as a client, so the door closes when the crown stops needing the town; the tell is the record of the grant and whether the door has ever been used; the fake that survives is the forged charter, which monastic houses produced in quantity and which the crown honored often enough when the forgery's side was the side it preferred, so a fake stands as long as the verifier wants it to be real; not register-jumps' carriers, which move a live situation into a new register, since here the jump is only threatened and its credibility is a document in a chest.

items.item: Meter on the walkaway: the option is credible in proportion to a visible quantity that depletes while it is displayed, as the strike fund whose balance the employer divides by weekly strike pay to get weeks, or the mobilized army whose daily cost the neighbor can estimate; the carrier is the fund or the payroll, and in the United States the union's annual filing makes the balance public; keeping it credible costs dues, or the standing cost of the mobilization, paid whether or not the option is used; the tell is the arithmetic, and a counterparty who can read the meter waits for it to run down rather than conceding to it; the fake that survives is the hidden reserve, a sympathy pledge from another union or an undisclosed credit line, which makes the meter read low on purpose; not runway-illusions' Watched burn, which is the operator's own life repriced by watchers, since here the metered quantity is the threat and the watcher is its target.
items.why: The tell is stated unconditionally, 'a counterparty who can read the meter waits for it to run down', but a meter reading thirty weeks against an employer who cannot survive six makes the employer concede, not wait; the meter is read against the counterparty's own pain, and the item's own near-term probe assumes both outcomes. One clause added; nothing else touched.
items.repair: Meter on the walkaway: the option is credible in proportion to a visible quantity that depletes while it is displayed, as the strike fund whose balance the employer divides by weekly strike pay to get weeks, or the mobilized army whose daily cost the neighbor can estimate; the carrier is the fund or the payroll, and in the United States the union's annual filing makes the balance public; keeping it credible costs dues, or the standing cost of the mobilization, paid whether or not the option is used; the tell is the arithmetic, and a counterparty who can read the meter and outlast it waits for it to run down rather than conceding to it, while one who cannot outlast it concedes to the number; the fake that survives is the hidden reserve, a sympathy pledge from another union or an undisclosed credit line, which makes the meter read low on purpose; not runway-illusions' Watched burn, which is the operator's own life repriced by watchers, since here the metered quantity is the threat and the watcher is its target.

items.item: Cheap to claim, ruinous to check: the walkaway destroys both parties, liquidation rather than a down round, the regulator rather than the settlement, the founder who leaves rather than takes the terms, and it is credible in proportion to a small probability of madness times a large loss, so it need not be likely to work; the carrier is the counterparty's estimate of what the holder has done to itself before; keeping it credible costs occasionally doing something ruinous, which is why the reputation is rarely maintained and the threat usually discounted; the tell is whether the holder has ever burned anything of its own, and a counterparty who finds nothing in the record calls it; the fake that survives is the one the counterparty cannot afford to test at any probability, because the concession is smaller than the expected ruin; not a walkaway to an alternative, since there is no alternative and the leaving is the point, which separates it from every other item here.
items.why: Kept as the speculative member it declares itself to be, but its discriminator's 'which separates it from every other item here' is false: Tied hands also has no alternative. Replaced with the real contrast, an excuse versus a threat, which also names the pair the incompatibility edge runs between.
items.repair: Cheap to claim, ruinous to check: the walkaway destroys both parties, liquidation rather than a down round, the regulator rather than the settlement, the founder who leaves rather than takes the terms, and it is credible in proportion to a small probability of madness times a large loss, so it need not be likely to work; the carrier is the counterparty's estimate of what the holder has done to itself before; keeping it credible costs occasionally doing something ruinous, which is why the reputation is rarely maintained and the threat usually discounted; the tell is whether the holder has ever burned anything of its own, and a counterparty who finds nothing in the record calls it; the fake that survives is the one the counterparty cannot afford to test at any probability, because the concession is smaller than the expected ruin; not a walkaway to an alternative, since there is no alternative and the leaving is the point, which it shares only with Tied hands, where the leaving is an excuse and here it is a threat.

items.item: Tied hands: unwillingness is converted into inability, as the negotiator whose board will not approve above a figure, the buyer whose policy forbids the term, the ransom negotiator who says the family has already sold the house, so the walkaway is a constraint persuasion cannot reach because its owner is not in the room; the carrier is the constraint's paper or its absent principal; keeping it credible costs consistency, since a party that later finds the money has revealed every future constraint as a choice; the tell is the constraint's edges, since a counterparty who asks for something the constraint does not cover finds that a real constraint yields easily there and a fake one resists everywhere; the fake that survives is the constraint whose owner cannot be reached, a policy nobody can produce, a board that does not meet; not Absent owner's clock, which borrows someone else's date, since this borrows someone else's refusal.
items.why: In type once the `of` is widened (see strongest_objection). It adjoins impasse-inventions' 'invented principal whose ratification buys distance and delay' more closely than anything it currently names, and the brief requires an adjacent item to say what it adds: a one-sided refusal meant to hold, not a shared delay chip. Discriminator extended; mechanism untouched.
items.repair: Tied hands: unwillingness is converted into inability, as the negotiator whose board will not approve above a figure, the buyer whose policy forbids the term, the ransom negotiator who says the family has already sold the house, so the walkaway is a constraint persuasion cannot reach because its owner is not in the room; the carrier is the constraint's paper or its absent principal; keeping it credible costs consistency, since a party that later finds the money has revealed every future constraint as a choice; the tell is the constraint's edges, since a counterparty who asks for something the constraint does not cover finds that a real constraint yields easily there and a fake one resists everywhere; the fake that survives is the constraint whose owner cannot be reached, a policy nobody can produce, a board that does not meet; not Absent owner's clock, which borrows someone else's date, since this borrows someone else's refusal; and not impasse-inventions' invented principal whose ratification buys distance and delay, a chip both sides adopt to break a deadlock, since here the principal belongs to one side and its refusal is meant to hold.

items.item: Absent owner's clock: a deadline whose owner is not at the table cannot be negotiated with the party who is, so the offer from elsewhere that expires Friday and the fund whose investment period ends in June import an urgency the table cannot soften; the carrier is the other party's calendar; keeping it credible costs letting it bind, since a clock named and then quietly extended discounts every clock the party names afterward; the tell is whether any deadline this party ever named was allowed to expire, and a request to see the offer with its date on it; the fake that survives is the clock the counterparty cannot watch expire, a private offer whose extension is never disclosed, which works exactly once per counterparty; not impasse-inventions' invented deadline, which both sides adopt to share urgency, since here the urgency is owned by someone who was never asked.
items.why: Modality: 'works exactly once per counterparty' is overprecise and quietly contradicts the clause before it (a clock the counterparty 'cannot watch expire'). What actually ends the fake is the counterparty seeing the party still seated after the named date; said so.
items.repair: Absent owner's clock: a deadline whose owner is not at the table cannot be negotiated with the party who is, so the offer from elsewhere that expires Friday and the fund whose investment period ends in June import an urgency the table cannot soften; the carrier is the other party's calendar; keeping it credible costs letting it bind, since a clock named and then quietly extended discounts every clock the party names afterward; the tell is whether any deadline this party ever named was allowed to expire, and a request to see the offer with its date on it; the fake that survives is the clock the counterparty cannot watch expire, a private offer whose extension is never disclosed, which works until the counterparty sees the party still seated after the date; not impasse-inventions' invented deadline, which both sides adopt to share urgency, since here the urgency is owned by someone who was never asked.

items.item: Silent floor: the option is known to the holder alone and works through what the holder will let die, as the employee whose spouse's income means the job is not necessary, so the counterparty sees a calm it cannot source; the carrier is the holder's own knowledge and the posture it produces; keeping it credible costs nothing, since it is never claimed, but a real floor also changes what the holder accepts while the fake changes only how the holder looks; the tell is the brink, since a party with a real floor lets the deal die there and a party without one folds in the last hour, so a counterparty who can afford one dead deal can sort them; the fake that survives is the rehearsed calm against a counterparty who cannot afford the brink, which is most of them; not negotiator-check-loops' walk-away rehearsal, the holder's inner check, since here the question is what the counterparty reads and at what price it can test.
items.why: Tested against Pawn-shop option by display: a spouse's income, once said aloud, still works or works better; an insider bridge, once said aloud, becomes a discount. They separate on the sign of display, so both stand.

items.item: Pawn-shop option: a real outside option that discredits its holder when shown, as the insider bridge that lets a founder refuse an outside lead's terms and that, once named, tells the lead the outsiders did not come, so a genuine alternative lowers the price it was meant to hold up; the carrier is the counterparty's reading of why the alternative is the alternative; keeping it credible costs silence, since the option is worth most while the counterparty does not know it exists, and its holder must refuse terms without saying what the refusal rests on; the tell is any mention of it, and a counterparty who suspects a bridge asks whether the insiders have already committed; the fake that survives is the unmentioned bridge, which works as a Silent floor until the day it is exercised and becomes a discount; not an option that fails when tested, since this one fails when displayed, and a line that sorts options by whether they must exist has no place for one that exists and must not be seen.
items.why: Survives the display test above and is the map's best strange member. Its endpoint position is earned by a different principle than the axis names (what showing does, not where it is held); noted under seriation, not a defect in the item.

items.item: Option they built for you: the counterparty supplies the option from its own prior, so the founder with the right resume is assumed to hold competing sheets and the surgeon assumed to hold offers, and the holder claims nothing; the carrier is the counterparty's model of the market and of the holder's kind; keeping it credible costs nothing while the prior holds and cannot be bought when it does not, since a claim would invite the check the prior spared; the tell is that there is none, because the counterparty never asks, and the option fails only when the prior updates, a down market, a public failure, a rival who checked; the fake that survives is the whole item, since no fake is manufactured, and a party who learns to look the part has built nothing and holds the strongest untested option on this map; not Silent floor, which the holder knows and the counterparty reads off posture, since here the holder may hold nothing and know it.
items.why: Speculative and declared so in mode and priorities; I was tempted to domesticate it into 'signaling kind' and did not, because the item's claim is stronger and stranger: nothing is signaled, the counterparty supplies the option and never tests it.

neighbor_test.separating_case: Both are alternatives held in another party's continuing willingness, both decay when the feeding stops, both cost a leak, and the author's own Kettle discriminator does not name Fed suitor, so they are the pair most tempting to merge as 'a rival kept interested'. Case one: a buyer moves fifteen percent of volume to a second supplier. The incumbent sees the loss on its own order book, so the upkeep is paid in the deal's currency and the counterparty can count it; the tell 'how much have they had?' is answerable from the incumbent's side. Case two: a founder takes quarterly coffee with an acquirer's corporate-development team. The investor sees nothing and can count nothing; the upkeep is information about the holder, paid to a third party, and that third party is holding the founder as its own option in return. Now convert: give the acquirer a paid pilot contract and the kettle becomes a fed suitor, because the acquirer is now receiving the deal's currency and the investor can see the revenue line. So the line between them is what is fed, not who is kept, and it is a line a party can cross on purpose; they do not collapse, but Kettle's discriminator had to be rewritten to say so.

boundary_case: The public floor: a seller who tells the press or the staff 'we will not sell below X', with no buyer in hand. Against the declared `of` it is out, since no alternative is built, borrowed, or faked. Against the fence the author actually uses in the burned-ships ruling (out because it makes staying credible), it is in, since it makes leaving credible by staking the holder's reputation before an audience, exactly the ground on which Tied hands and Cheap to claim are in. It is not Second table in the square, where the square is the destination; here the square is only the witness. It is not Walk on record, which is a walk already taken. Ruling: the correct fence is 'makes staying credible' out and 'makes leaving credible' in, which is why the `of` must widen; and boundary_claim four, which files 'the precommitment' beside burned ships, should file only the precommitment to fight there. The public floor is then a member the map lacks, held in the holder's reputation between Walk on record and Tied hands; I do not add it, but the repairer should not read boundary_claim four as excluding it.

seriation.note: Endpoints are real: Nothing to leave needs no believer, Pawn-shop option needs the counterparty's ignorance. Qualified on paper to Fed suitor teaches (re-qualification money for a share of business; the tell moves from a date to an amount). The middle run from Rented war chest through Higher court's door (money, calendar, jurisdiction) and the late run from Silent floor through Cheap to claim (holder alone, absent principal, confederate, the checker's bill, the checker's ruin) read as increasing distance from the holder and are defensible as an itinerary. One caveat the author half-concedes: Silent floor (twelfth, 'the holder's own knowledge') and Pawn-shop option (last, 'the counterparty's ignorance') are the same place seen from two sides, so the final stop is not a new location; the endpoint is earned by what display does to the option, which the note admits with 'the axis of existence runs out'. That is honest and the walk still teaches, so no reorder.

edges.to_handle: Cheap to claim, ruinous to check
edges.why: As written the incompatibility is unconditional ('past a point one party cannot hold both') and the map's own ransom case refutes it: a family that cannot pay more and can still call the police holds both in one room, because the constraint and the ruin have different owners. The incompatibility is real only when the absent owner who ties the hands also owns the ruinous act, as when a board that will not approve a price also controls liquidation; the antecedent must say so, and then it can fail.
edges.repair_label: If the absent owner whose refusal ties the party's hands also owns the act that would burn both sides, as when the board that will not approve the price is the body that would have to vote liquidation, the party cannot in the same room make its walkaway a willingness to burn, since the constraint that excuses the refusal denies it the agency the burning needs, and a counterparty who hears both knows one is manufactured; where the constraint and the ruin have different owners, the family that cannot pay more and can still call the police, both stand.

edges.why: Inherits the Meter item's unconditional tell: a readable meter makes the counterparty wait only if the counterparty can outlast it. Conditioned to match the repaired item; the passage from displayed to hidden is kept.
edges.repair_label: If the counterparty can read the meter and outlast it, it waits for the quantity to run down instead of conceding, so a party whose meter reads shorter than the counterparty's pain must hide the reserve, and the hidden reserve works only as a silent floor, at the brink and never by display; the metered option recruits a silent one and cannot be shown again without a new meter.

edges.why: I tried to break the loop by noting that a lapsed outside offer is a walk from the other table, not from this one. It survives: Walk on record's record keeps outcomes, not motives, and a party seen losing an alternative rather than extending a clock has bought an entry without the upkeep the item names (walking from a deal it wanted). That is the edge's actual claim and it is a real one; a bare sequence would not show it.

modality_problems: Higher court's door: 'the crown honored [forged charters] whenever the forgery's side was the side it preferred' asserts a universal about medieval verification that the record does not support; repaired to 'often enough'.
Absent owner's clock: 'works exactly once per counterparty' is a precise-sounding claim with no basis and contradicts the clause before it; repaired.
Meter on the walkaway and the edge Meter → Silent floor: 'a counterparty who can read the meter waits' is stated as a law and holds only when the counterparty can outlast the meter; repaired in both.

Edge Tied hands → Cheap to claim: an incompatibility asserted without a condition and refuted by the map's own ransom case; repaired to name the condition (one owner for both the constraint and the ruin).
Cheap to claim, ruinous to check: 'which separates it from every other item here' is false (Tied hands shares the no-alternative shape); repaired.

boundary_claim four lumps 'the precommitment' with burned ships as out-of-type; a precommitment to fight is out, a precommitment to leave is in-type and merely absent. The repairer should narrow that clause to 'the burned ships, the precommitment to fight'.
Fed suitor's 'the third time it learns' and Paid floor's 'a few percent of the price' are illustrative figures that read as illustrative; no change.
duplication: No existing grown list covers manufactured walkaways as a whole. Adjacencies the author already discriminates: Silent floor against negotiator-check-loops' walk-away rehearsal; Absent owner's clock against impasse-inventions' invented deadline and exploding intermediate; Paid floor against power-trades' Fence around the process; Higher court's door against register-jumps; Nothing to leave and Rented war chest against survival-floors. One adjacency the author missed and the brief requires: Tied hands against impasse-inventions' 'invented principal whose ratification buys distance and delay', repaired into its discriminator. Rented war chest is also near survival-floors' Kept on call ('a floor that is really an option someone else holds'), but the mechanism differs (the funder owns the walkaway and is paid from the win), so no change.
best_unresolved_seed: The walkaway the counterparty pays for. Severance, change-of-control acceleration, and the reverse termination fee all make the holder's leaving cheap with money from the party it will be used against, agreed at signing when the state seemed improbable (power-trades' Veto sold as an improbability run in reverse). Its existence is held in the counterparty's own paper, a stop the axis 'where the alternative's existence is held' does not have; its tell is the counterparty's own signature, so there is no fake to detect and no check to run; and it may be the only walkaway whose credibility rises when displayed, since showing it reminds the counterparty what it already agreed to pay. That would give Pawn-shop option an opposite number and turn the map's last step into an axis of its own: what display does to the option's price.
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after widening the declared type to cover a leaving that needs no alternative, which two kept items already required, repairing seven item clauses (an upkeep slot holding the exercise cost, a discriminator naming a non-item, a charter-forgery 'whenever', an unconditional meter tell, a false uniqueness claim, a missed adjacency to impasse-inventions, an overprecise 'exactly once'), and conditioning two edge labels whose antecedents could not fail as written.
